Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. messages.content:
The issue is likely caused by the wrapping logic in the `printHelp` method of the `HelpFormatter` class in Apache Commons CLI. The method `printHelp` is responsible for generating the help text with the specified formatting.

1. The `printHelp` method takes various parameters including the width for the text, command line syntax, header, options, padding values, and footer.
2. Within the method, it first checks if `cmdLineSyntax` is provided and throws an exception if not.
3. It then checks if `autoUsage` is enabled, and based on that, either calls `printUsage` with additional parameters or a simpler version of `printUsage`.
4. Next, it prints the `header` if it is not null and has non-whitespace characters.
5. It then prints the options with the specified left padding and description padding.
6. Finally, it prints the `footer` if it is not null and has non-whitespace characters.

The bug report describes an issue where if there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, the `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes with an OutOfMemoryError. This behavior is likely occurring in the wrapping logic implemented in the `printHelp` method.

Next, I will suggest potential methods to be fixed based on this diagnosis.
The issue can be resolved by fixing the logic in the following methods:

1. `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options,int,int,java.lang.String)` 
2. `org.apache.commons.cli.HelpFormatter.printHelp(java.io.PrintWriter,int,java.lang.String,java.lang.String,org.apache.commons.cli.Options,int,int,java.lang.String,boolean)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
